description: F-KLR-001: which costing runs exist is answerable. `costAllocationSheet`, `overheadRates` and `productionCost` all require a `runId` and no projection said where one comes from — the only way to hold a valid id was to have kept the one `runCosting` returned. So an embedding kept its own table of run ids beside the books, which is a second register of library state and drifts with the first change that does not pass through the screen that writes it; the audit log was the other shortcut, and rebuilding library state from a trail is what F-13 already named as a bug in waiting. The repository has had a sorted `all()` since the runs were persisted, so this was a published-surface gap, not a design boundary. Deliberately thin: what a run IS — id, period, version, status, method — and nothing it computed, because a total repeated here would be a second answer to a question the three projections above already answer. Reported by an embedding application as its F-24.

steps.comment: Two runs over the same period: the second is version 2, and both stay listed — a superseded draft is part of the period's history.

expect.comment: Ohne Filter: alles, was es gibt, sortiert nach Periode und dann Version — die Reihenfolge, in der die nächste Version entsteht und in der eine Periodenhistorie gelesen wird.
Eine Periode ohne Läufe ist leer, kein Fehler — „es gibt keine" ist eine Antwort.
